page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It contains no local storage and does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge delivers modest processing capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. Memory bandwidth performance varies, with small-block read-only operations ranking in the bottom 25%, while large-block read and write operations achieve average performance in the middle 50% tier. Cryptographic and database operations, such as Redis SET and PassMark database tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25%.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation but older Intel Broadwell architecture, the instance offers stable but lower-tier compute density. It is suitable for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without demanding high-frequency execution, such as basic web serving, lightweight software compilation, or small-scale LLM inference tasks using models under 135M parameters. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into the architectural design.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance utilizing an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance features no local storage and has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the lower tiers, with stress-ng and Geekbench CPU scores falling in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. However, uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth reaches average levels. Lacking local storage and GPU acceleration, this instance is best suited for workloads with moderate computational requirements, such as basic web serving, lightweight software compilation, and small-scale text processing or minor model inference tasks where dedicated CPU allocation is preferred over shared-core alternatives.
